modules.title: Foundation Building
modules.description: Money market fundamentals, lending math, risk basics, and first positions

questions.question: How do DeFi money markets differ from traditional bank lending?

options.text: DeFi requires branch visits and credit scores
DeFi uses smart contracts and overcollateralization instead of credit underwriting

questions.explanation: DeFi lending is typically permissionless and collateral-based, with rates set by supply/demand on-chain.

questions.question: What does Health Factor (HF) measure?

options.text: How far your collateralized position is from liquidation
The age of a smart contract

questions.explanation: Health Factor combines collateral value, debt, and liquidation thresholds — lower HF means higher liquidation risk.

questions.question: What happens when utilization of a lending pool is very high?

options.text: Borrow rates tend to increase to incentivize new supply
Supply APY always goes to zero

questions.explanation: High utilization means scarce borrowable liquidity — interest rate models typically raise borrow rates to attract deposits.

questions.question: Why do beginners often start with stablecoin collateral on Layer 2?

options.text: Lower volatility and fees make learning safer and cheaper

questions.explanation: Stable collateral reduces price swing risk while L2 lowers transaction costs for practice positions.

questions.question: What is Loan-to-Value (LTV)?

options.text: The maximum borrow amount relative to collateral value at origination
The gas fee for a transaction
The number of validators on a chain
The funding rate on a perpetual swap

questions.explanation: LTV caps how much you can borrow against deposited collateral — distinct from liquidation threshold.

modules.title: Intermediate Strategies
modules.description: Advanced position management, rate dynamics, and multi-protocol workflows

questions.question: What is the difference between LTV and Liquidation Threshold?

options.text: LTV is max borrow at open; liquidation threshold is the point where collateral can be seized
Liquidation threshold is always lower than LTV

questions.explanation: You borrow up to LTV, but liquidation occurs when collateral value breaches the higher liquidation threshold buffer.

questions.question: Why monitor oracle price feeds when managing borrow positions?

options.text: Oracles determine collateral valuations used for liquidations

questions.explanation: Protocols rely on oracles for asset prices — stale or manipulated feeds can trigger unexpected liquidations.

questions.question: What is a common use of borrowed stablecoins in DeFi?

options.text: Leverage or liquidity deployment while keeping collateral exposure

questions.explanation: Borrowers often use debt for additional yield strategies — which increases complexity and liquidation risk.

questions.question: What does 'rate arbitrage' between protocols involve?

options.text: Exploiting differences in supply/borrow rates across platforms with matched risk awareness

questions.explanation: Rate differentials can create opportunities but carry smart contract, bridge, and liquidation risks.

questions.question: Why maintain a health factor buffer above the minimum?

options.text: To absorb collateral price drops before liquidation
Protocols require HF of exactly 1.0 at all times

questions.explanation: Buffers account for volatility and interest accrual — operating near liquidation is fragile.

modules.title: Advanced Mastery
modules.description: Complex strategies, protocol comparison, and institutional-style risk frameworks

questions.question: What is isolation mode in some lending protocols?

options.text: A feature that limits new assets to separate risk silos so they cannot endanger the entire pool
A marketing term with no technical meaning

questions.explanation: Isolation contains tail risk from newer or volatile collateral types.

questions.question: What risk does recursive borrowing (leverage looping) introduce?

options.text: Amplified exposure — small price moves can cascade into rapid liquidation

questions.explanation: Each loop multiplies effective leverage, compressing the margin before liquidation.

questions.question: When comparing money market protocols, what should you evaluate beyond APY?

options.text: Audit history, oracle design, governance, liquidity, and liquidation parameters

questions.explanation: Yield is one input — security architecture and risk parameters determine survivability.

questions.question: What is e-mode (efficiency mode) on some lending platforms?

options.text: Higher LTV for correlated assets within a defined category, with stricter asset grouping

questions.explanation: E-mode increases capital efficiency for correlated collateral (e.g. stables) while limiting composability across categories.

questions.question: What is a professional approach to DeFi money market risk?

options.text: Document scenarios, stress-test HF, diversify protocols, and define exit rules before entering
Max leverage whenever APY is high
Use unaudited forks for highest yields only

questions.explanation: Systematic risk frameworks — not yield chasing alone — define sustainable money market participation.
